findings.finding: The `DetGateRule` schema has a single `text_re: str | None` field, but the asserted-capability trigger is a CONJUNCTION of two independent regex legs (module-ref AND capability-verb). Baking a conjunction into one regex requires a lookahead (`(?=.*module-ref)(?=.*capability-verb)`) that makes the regex substantially more complex and harder to audit/test. The plan does not state whether the conjunction is expressed as a lookahead-based single regex, as two `text_re` fields, or as a different schema extension. This is an underspecification that can lead the implementer to choose an incompatible approach.

findings.finding: The plan changes observable behavior — plans that previously received LLM routing for T13, T14, removal-rationale, and asserted-capability will now be silently skipped when triggers don't fire — but provides no rollback path, feature flag, or expand-contract sequencing if production false-negative rates exceed the 743-ticket audit's estimates.
findings.location: Approach section (pre-filter contract); ADR 0034 Relationship section
scenarios: A class of plans not covered by the 743-ticket audit (e.g., domain-specific jargon, future feature areas) systematically evades the trigger and receives no LLM review for these criteria — there is no stated monitoring or rollback to detect or recover from this.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Add an explicit unit test asserting that a plan matching ONLY the module-ref leg (no capability-verb) and a plan matching ONLY the capability-verb leg (no module-ref) each skip asserted-capability with a coverage entry, verifying the AND conjunction is enforced.
evidence: 'asserted-capability: conjunction of module-ref leg … AND capability-verb leg' — plan Approach section
AC1 only tests that evasion sentences fire, not that partial matches (one leg only) correctly skip
No test described for 'module-ref leg matches, capability-verb leg does not → skip' or vice versa
findings.finding: The asserted-capability trigger is a CONJUNCTION of two regex legs (module-ref AND capability-verb), but the testing plan only verifies that 'all audit evasion sentences fire their trigger' — it does not include a test for the partial-match case where only one leg matches and the criterion must NOT fire (skip). This leaves the conjunction semantics untested against the most natural regression (a plan that mentions a module name but no capability verb, or vice versa).
findings.location: Testing section / AC line 1: 'All audit evasion sentences fire their respective triggers'
scenarios: A plan mentioning a module name (e.g. 'utils.py') but no capability-verb fires asserted-capability erroneously, sending unnecessary LLM traffic — the opposite of the plan's goal.
A regex bug that ORs rather than ANDs the legs would pass the 'evasion sentences fire' test but fail the partial-match test, shipping silently.
findings.suggested_fix: In test_det_criterion_gates.py, add two parametrized negative cases for asserted-capability: (1) plan text containing only a module reference ('src/rebar/utils.py is updated') with no capability-verb → expect skip; (2) plan text containing only a capability-verb ('the feature already exists') with no module-ref pattern → expect skip. Both should assert zero LLM routing and a coverage skip entry.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Consider externalizing the DetGateRule regex/glob/deletion fields to criteria_routing.json (or a dedicated det_gates.json) so trigger tuning is a config change rather than a Python source edit, given the plan already acknowledges these patterns required post-audit amendment.
evidence: 'Rule schema: a DetGateRule dataclass {text_re: str | None, file_impact_globs: list[str], requires_declared_deletion: bool}' — defined in Python, not JSON
'Trigger regexes (case-insensitive; transcribed from the audit, provenance ticket 696a)' — transcribed into source
'the draft narrower regexes — the audit demonstrated realistic evasion classes for each' — acknowledged prior revision, implying future revision is plausible
criteria_routing.json receives only 'trigger annotations', not the actual regex payloads
findings.finding: The large, complex trigger regexes (T13, T14, removal-rationale, asserted-capability) are hardcoded in Python source (DetGateRule dataclass instances in registry.py/_DET_OVERLAY_RULES/_DET_LEAF_GATE_RULES). The plan explicitly acknowledges these regexes needed post-hoc widening once already (the audit amended draft triggers for evasion classes), signaling continued evolution is expected. No mention is made of externalizing them to criteria_routing.json or another config surface — a future tuning round requires a Python source edit, review, and re-deploy rather than a config update.
findings.location: Approach section — DetGateRule dataclass / registry.py scope; Trigger regexes block
scenarios: Next evasion-class discovery requires a regex change → full code-review/deploy cycle instead of a config bump
Regex ownership is split between the audit record (ticket 696a) and the source file, making provenance tracking harder
findings.suggested_fix: Move the four DetGateRule definitions into criteria_routing.json under a `det_gate` key per criterion; load them in registry.py at startup. This keeps the Python dataclass as a typed loader/validator and makes future regex tuning a config PR without touching application logic.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Extend the ADR 0034 amendment note (or AGENTS.md) to document the overlay-vs-leaf-gate routing rule for criterion authors — specifically: overlay criteria (registry.is_overlay == True) use _DET_OVERLAY_RULES; leaf-routed criteria use _DET_LEAF_GATE_RULES and the second orchestrator block.
evidence: 'T13 and T14 are overlay criteria … extend the existing _DET_OVERLAY_RULES path'; 'removal-rationale and asserted-capability are leaf-routed, NOT overlays, so they get a parallel _DET_LEAF_GATE_RULES table plus a second gate block'
ADR amendment described as stating 'the pre-filter's contract' only — no mention of overlay-vs-leaf routing rule for criterion authors
'sizing.py's is_overlay call sites are audited for the new table' — signals this distinction has real behavioral consequences
AGENTS.md is absent from the Scope list
findings.finding: The plan introduces a new duality — overlay criteria gate through the existing _DET_OVERLAY_RULES block, while leaf criteria gate through a new _DET_LEAF_GATE_RULES table and a second block in orchestrator.route_criteria — but the ADR 0034 amendment note is described only as stating 'the pre-filter's contract (skip only on total vocabulary absence; the LLM router remains the applicability authority for fired plans).' The rule governing which path a future new criterion takes (overlay vs. leaf-gate) is not described as being documented anywhere for criterion authors, leaving it as implicit source-code knowledge.
findings.location: Approach section — overlay/leaf gate distinction; ADR 0034 amendment note description; Scope
scenarios: A contributor adds a new leaf-routed criterion and mistakenly registers it in _DET_OVERLAY_RULES (or vice versa), producing silently incorrect gating
The overlay/leaf distinction is only discoverable by reading orchestrator.py source, not from the ADR or AGENTS.md
findings.suggested_fix: Add a 'Adding a new det-gated criterion' subsection to either the ADR 0034 amendment or AGENTS.md listing: (1) check registry.is_overlay; (2) if True, add a DetGateRule to _DET_OVERLAY_RULES; (3) if False, add to _DET_LEAF_GATE_RULES. Keep it to ~5 lines.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Verify that `PlanContext`/`ctx.state` carries a structured per-file `file_impact` list (with individual paths and delete/modify flags) accessible at the `route_criteria` seam, or specify what data-threading changes to `PlanContext` are required to make the T14 glob arm and the removal-rationale deletion arm work.
evidence: Plan: 'overlay_triggers gains an optional file_impact parameter threaded from route_criteria'
Existing orchestrator.py:344: `triggers = registry.overlay_triggers(plan)` — only `plan` is passed; no file_impact argument exists today
Existing orchestrator.py:378: `file_impact_scope=ctx.state.get('file_impact_scope')` — only a scope string is extracted, not a list of individual paths
registry.py:389-415: `applies()` likewise only receives `file_impact_scope: str | None`, never a file list
ABSENCE: no evidence in the plan or codebase that PlanContext/ctx.state carries individual file paths with delete/modify flags accessible at the route_criteria seam
findings.finding: The plan asserts that `overlay_triggers` will gain an optional `file_impact` parameter 'threaded from route_criteria,' and that T14's glob arm and removal-rationale's deletion arm will fire on `file_impact` paths alone — but it is unverified whether `route_criteria`'s input (`PlanContext`/`ctx.state`) carries individual file-impact paths (with per-file delete/modify flags) rather than just the `file_impact_scope` string that the existing code accesses.
findings.location: Approach section — 'overlay_triggers gains an optional file_impact parameter threaded from route_criteria'; Acceptance Criteria — 'The T14 glob arm and the removal-rationale deletion arm fire on file_impact alone'
scenarios: T14 glob arm (.github/workflows match) silently fails because the file-path list is not threaded through to overlay_triggers, meaning the glob arm never fires on file_impact alone — contradicting AC3.
removal-rationale deletion arm never fires on declared deletions if the per-file delete flag is not accessible at the routing seam, silently leaving the deletion OR-arm inoperative.
findings.suggested_fix: Add a 'Data availability' sub-section to the Approach that either (a) cites the specific `PlanContext` field that already carries individual file paths and deletion flags, or (b) lists `PlanContext` as an in-scope change to add a `file_impact_paths: list[str]` and `has_declared_deletion: bool` field threaded from `ctx.state`.

findings.finding: The plan reverses ADR 0034's explicit design decision to use LLM-routed (not lexical) triggers for T13 and T14, without addressing the ADR's stated rationale. ADR 0034 (docs/adr/0034-llm-routed-enumeration-overlays.md) documents that 'a lexical trigger over-fires on descriptive prose; the LLM router decides applicability' — the plan now proposes lexical triggers for T13/T14 without reconciling this or superseding the ADR.
findings.location: Approach section / Trigger regexes section — T13/T14 entries
findings.suggested_fix: Add a brief section citing ADR 0034 and stating why the audit evidence (84% / 61.6% fire rates with precision-recall trade-off documented) resolves the original over-fire concern. Update the trigger annotations in criteria_routing.json from 'LLM-routed' to 'DET-gated' as part of the deliverable.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Specify that a DetGateRule evaluation error is fail-open: a raising gate check is treated as 'fired' (routes to the LLM) rather than aborting routing, and the error is logged + recorded in the coverage skip entry.
evidence: det_invariants.py:_run_one: every project DET criterion is wrapped in try/except that converts a raising check to an 'abstain' DetResult
route_criteria (orchestrator.py:340–398): no try/except around the existing gate blocks; a new gate block similarly has no specified error handling
T13 trigger regex is ~700 chars; T14 text regex is ~850 chars — a subtle syntax error (e.g. unbalanced group from a future edit) would raise `re.error` at evaluation time
Plan: 'a not-fired rule skips the criterion … a fired rule routes to the LLM exactly as today' — no third case (evaluation error) is addressed
findings.finding: No fail-open fallback is specified for an exception raised during `DetGateRule` evaluation (e.g. a regex compile error on the very long trigger patterns, or a glob-match error). The existing DET floor wraps every check in try/except (det_invariants.py `run_project_det_checks`); `route_criteria` itself has no such guard and an unhandled exception would abort criterion routing entirely for the ticket.
findings.location: Approach section — gate block description; Testing section — no mention of exception path
scenarios: A regex compile error on first call raises re.error inside route_criteria, aborting all criterion routing for the ticket (no LLM review runs at all)
A glob-match TypeError (e.g. None in file_impact_paths) propagates out of the leaf-gate block and produces an unsigned INDETERMINATE verdict
findings.suggested_fix: Add to the Approach: 'Gate evaluation is fail-open: any exception during DetGateRule.matches() is caught, logged, and treated as fired (the criterion routes to the LLM as if the gate had not been installed).'
